security_guidelines.overview: Zero-trust security practices for dotfiles automation and shell scripting. These guidelines ensure scripts are secure by default and protect against common attack vectors.

principle.name: least_privilege
principle.description: Scripts should request only the minimum permissions necessary. Never run scripts as root unless absolutely required.

implementation.rule: Never use sudo in scripts unless explicitly documented
Use user-level installations when possible (e.g., --user flag)
Install to user directories (~/.local/bin) not system directories
Fail gracefully when elevated permissions are unavailable

principle.code_example:
# Prefer user-local installations install_binary() { local binary="$1" local install_dir="${HOME}/.local/bin"
# Ensure user bin directory exists mkdir -p "$install_dir"
# Install to user directory, not /usr/local/bin mv "$binary" "$install_dir/" chmod 755 "$install_dir/$binary"
# Ensure PATH includes user bin if [[ ":$PATH:" != *":$install_dir:"* ]]; then log_warning "Add $install_dir to your PATH" fi }

principle.name: input_validation
principle.description: Never trust input from any source - environment variables, arguments, files, or network resources.

implementation.rule: Validate all environment variables before use
Sanitize file paths to prevent traversal attacks
Use allowlists, not denylists for validation
Quote all variable expansions

principle.code_example:
# Validate environment variable validate_path() { local path="${1:-}"
# Reject empty paths if [[ -z "$path" ]]; then log_error "Path cannot be empty" return 1 fi
# Reject path traversal attempts if [[ "$path" == *".."* ]]; then log_error "Path traversal not allowed" return 1 fi
# Reject absolute paths outside expected areas if [[ "$path" == /* ]] && [[ "$path" != "$HOME"* ]] && [[ "$path" != "/tmp"* ]]; then log_error "Path must be within home directory or /tmp" return 1 fi
# Validate characters (allowlist approach) if [[ ! "$path" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_./-]+$ ]]; then log_error "Path contains invalid characters" return 1 fi
return 0 }

principle.name: secret_management
principle.description: Never store secrets in scripts, environment files, or version control. Use secure secret management practices.

implementation.rule: Never hardcode passwords, tokens, or API keys
Use environment variables from secure sources
Prefer secret managers (1Password CLI, pass, etc.)
Add .env files to .gitignore
Use .env.example with placeholder values only

principle.code_example:
# Secure secret retrieval pattern get_secret() { local secret_name="${1:?Secret name required}"
# Priority: secret manager > environment > prompt if command -v op &>/dev/null; then # 1Password CLI op read "op://Private/${secret_name}" 2>/dev/null && return 0 fi
if command -v pass &>/dev/null; then # pass (password-store) pass show "${secret_name}" 2>/dev/null && return 0 fi
# Fall back to environment variable (should be set securely) local env_var env_var=$(echo "$secret_name" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]' | tr '-' '_') if [[ -n "${!env_var:-}" ]]; then echo "${!env_var}" return 0 fi
# Interactive prompt (last resort) if [[ -t 0 ]]; then read -rsp "Enter ${secret_name}: " secret echo >&2 echo "$secret" return 0 fi
log_error "Cannot retrieve secret: $secret_name" return 1 }
# Example: .env.example (committed to git) # DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:password@localhost:5432/db # API_KEY=your-api-key-here

principle.name: safe_defaults
principle.description: Default behavior should be the safest option. Destructive or risky operations should require explicit opt-in.

implementation.rule: Default to dry-run mode for destructive operations
Require confirmation for irreversible actions
Create backups before modifying existing files
Use --force or similar flags for override, never default

principle.code_example:
# Safe removal with backup safe_remove() { local target="${1:?Target required}" local force="${2:-false}" local backup_dir="${HOME}/.trash"
if [[ ! -e "$target" ]]; then log_info "Target does not exist: $target" return 0 fi
# Require confirmation unless forced if [[ "$force" != "true" ]]; then read -rp "Remove $target? [y/N] " confirm if [[ ! "$confirm" =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then log_info "Skipped: $target" return 0 fi fi
# Create backup mkdir -p "$backup_dir" local backup_name backup_name="${backup_dir}/$(basename "$target").$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)" mv "$target" "$backup_name" log_success "Moved to backup: $backup_name" }

principle.name: supply_chain_security
principle.description: Protect against compromised dependencies and supply chain attacks. Use custom forks for security-critical tools.

implementation.rule: Fork security-critical tools to personal repositories
Verify checksums for downloaded binaries
Pin specific versions, avoid "latest"
Review code changes before updating forks
Use GPG-signed commits and releases when available

principle.code_example:
# Installing from custom fork with verification install_from_fork() { local repo="$1" # e.g., "username/fzf" local version="$2" # e.g., "v0.44.0" local binary="$3" # e.g., "fzf" local checksum="$4" # SHA256 checksum
local url="https://github.com/${repo}/releases/download/${version}/${binary}"
# Download to temp location local temp_file temp_file=$(mktemp) trap 'rm -f "$temp_file"' RETURN
log_step "Downloading ${binary} from trusted fork..." curl -fsSL "$url" -o "$temp_file"
# Verify checksum local actual_sum actual_sum=$(sha256sum "$temp_file" | cut -d' ' -f1) if [[ "$actual_sum" != "$checksum" ]]; then log_error "Checksum verification failed!" log_error "Expected: $checksum" log_error "Got: $actual_sum" return 1 fi
log_success "Checksum verified" install_binary "$temp_file" "$binary" }
# Example: Installing fzf from custom fork # install_from_fork "marcelocra/fzf" "v0.44.0" "fzf-linux-amd64" \ # "abc123def456..."

category.name: script_review
category.item: No hardcoded secrets, tokens, or passwords
No unnecessary sudo or root requirements

category.name: environment_review
category.item: Appropriate file permissions (600 for secrets, 755 for scripts)

vulnerability.name: shell_injection
vulnerability.example_bad: # DANGEROUS: If user_input contains "; rm -rf /" eval "process $user_input"

vulnerability.name: path_traversal
vulnerability.description: User input used directly in file paths
vulnerability.example_good: # Safe: Validate and sanitize validate_filename() { local name="$1" [[ "$name" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$ ]] && [[ "$name" != *".."* ]] } if validate_filename "$user_file"; then cat "$config_dir/$user_file" fi

vulnerability.name: insecure_temp_files
vulnerability.description: Predictable temporary file names allow attacks
vulnerability.example_bad: # DANGEROUS: Predictable path, race condition echo "data" > /tmp/myapp.tmp
vulnerability.example_good: # Safe: Use mktemp with cleanup temp_file=$(mktemp) trap 'rm -f "$temp_file"' EXIT echo "data" > "$temp_file"

vulnerability.name: curl_pipe_bash
vulnerability.description: Piping curl to bash without verification
vulnerability.example_bad: # DANGEROUS: No verification curl -fsSL https://example.com/install.sh | bash
vulnerability.example_good: # Better: Download, review, then execute curl -fsSL https://example.com/install.sh -o install.sh # Review the script less install.sh # Verify checksum if provided echo "expected_sha256 install.sh" | sha256sum -c # Then execute bash install.sh
